object_description: square, flat building volume organized around two courtyards
design_condition: The square, flat structure is placed on Flurstrasse to open a generous outdoor space toward the Bachwiesen sports center and connect the surrounding green areas into a continuous belt.

positive.statement: The classic horizontal tripartite division and structural dichotomy reflected in the façade structure the building well and harmoniously.

position.rationale: Regular horizontal façade bands and the square envelope are visible in the elevations.

positive.statement: The cluster units are well functioning and arranged around two covered inner courtyards.

position.rationale: The courtyard-centered organization is inferred within the visible square perimeter.

positive.statement: The chosen structure provides a very high degree of long-term flexibility.

position.rationale: Flexibility concerns the distributed structural building system across the sampled envelope.

positive.statement: The outdoor space integrates the school grounds harmoniously and transparently into their surroundings.

position.rationale: The surrounding outdoor integration is approximated along the building’s southern-western site edge.

positive.statement: The project impresses with its stringent, conceptual approach.

position.rationale: The conceptual statement addresses the complete compact square building.

negative.statement: The placement of certain ancillary rooms along the internal street is incomprehensible.

position.rationale: Internal ancillary-room placement is approximated along the inferred central circulation zone.

negative.statement: The communal spaces have no direct, ground-floor connection to the outside.

position.rationale: Ground-floor communal access is constrained to a plausible southern building surface.

negative.statement: The concrete slats are potentially expensive to produce and generate additional unusable room heights.

position.rationale: Repeated horizontal façade elements are visible across the south elevation.

negative.statement: The structural feasibility of the connections between the slats and the outer wall remains an open question.

position.rationale: The connection detail is not distinguishable, so it is anchored to the visible slatted façade.

negative.statement: The fragmented situation in the central schoolyard with the double path and stairs has not been resolved.

position.rationale: The unresolved central yard circulation is placed within the apparent interior courtyard zone.

negative.statement: The character of the building is perceived as off-putting and too autonomous, raising questions about its expression for an elementary school.

position.rationale: Character and autonomy are judgments about the complete visible building mass.

negative.statement: Access via the ramp is very narrow and contradicts the idea of a school building for small children.

position.rationale: Access is anchored to a plausible low southern-western edge location; the ramp is not separately visible.
